description: A bespoke XML editor for dreaming Hybrasyl worlds into reality
author: Sabrael (http://www.github.com/Caeldeth)
_overridesNote: brace-expansion carries a high-severity DoS advisory (GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg). It reaches
us only through dev tooling -- eslint, eslint-plugin-react, electron-builder -- so
nothing that ships is affected.
The advisory is patched WITHIN EVERY MAJOR: 1.1.17, 2.1.3, 3.0.3, 5.0.8. Our 2.x and
5.x copies already resolve at or above their patched version, so only the 1.x copies
(pinned by minimatch 3.x) need moving, and they only need to move to 1.1.18.
The override is SCOPED to `brace-expansion@1` on purpose. A bare `brace-expansion`
override drags every consumer to 5.x, which CHANGED ITS EXPORT SHAPE: 1.x/2.x are
`module.exports = expandTop`, 5.x is `module.exports = { expand, ... }`. minimatch 3.x
does `var expand = require('brace-expansion')` and calls it, so a bare override dies
with `TypeError: expand is not a function` -- but ONLY for a pattern containing braces,
because minimatch 3.x short-circuits braceExpand for patterns without them. Our eslint
config globs `**/*.{js,jsx,mjs,cjs}`, so we would hit it on the first lint; a config
with no braces passes and ships the landmine instead.
Scoping keeps each major on its own line: minimatch 3.x keeps a default-export 1.1.18,
minimatch 10.x keeps brace-expansion 5.x, whose named `expand` it imports. No
@eslint/config-array pin is needed, and nothing has to come back out when eslint 10
lands -- the selector simply stops matching when the last minimatch 3.x consumer goes.
Verified: eslint still reports a seeded violation (not silently matching zero files),
and minimatch 3.x expands `**/*.{js,jsx,mjs,cjs}` correctly under 1.1.18.
